sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Lrp6-APEX2 chimeric receptor (carrying N-terminal VSV-G) rescued the ventralized phenotype caused by maternal depletion of Xenopus Lrp6 and induced axis duplication in a ligand-dependent manner when overexpressed in a ventral blastomere; surface display confirmed by translocation of the tagged receptor into cytoplasmic vesicles upon Wnt3a treatment.
sites.rationale: L5 explicitly states the full-length human Lrp6 construct carries an N-terminal VSV-G tag; because the extracellular domain begins at residue 20 (after the native SP cleavage at 1–19), the VSV-G tag is placed at the same junction as the FLAG tag in L1/L2: insert_after_residue=19, residue_before=A (pos 19), residue_after=A (pos 20), confirmed by Python lookup. L4 demonstrates the doubly-tagged construct is fully functional in a stringent in vivo assay, and L6 confirms surface display. This is a second independent paper (PMC7726150 vs PMC8980801) validating the same extracellular N-terminal junction with a different tag, warranting a separate site entry at higher validation level. Full-length human Lrp6 membrane-anchored construct bearing an N-terminal VSV-G tag (extracellular) and a C-terminal linker-FLAG–APEX2 fusion (intracellular). Surface display of the VSV-G-tagged receptor confirmed (L6). Functional rescue of ventralized Xenopus embryos and ligand-dependent axis duplication confirmed for this doubly-tagged construct (PMC7726150).

sources.claim: The human Lrp6 contains an N-terminal VSV-G and a linker Flag-tag followed by the APEX2 enzyme.

Human LRP6 (residues 20–1613), with an N-terminal hemagglutinin signal peptide followed immediately by a FLAG tag, and a C-terminal His 8 tag, was first subcloned into pcDNA3.1 (Invitrogen); this was truncated at residue 1439 by overlap extension PCR.

literature_notes: All six ledger lines concern a single junction: the mature N-terminus of LRP6 (after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 19). L1/L2 (PMC8980801) report a FLAG tag there with surface confirmation; L5/L6 (PMC7726150) report a VSV-G tag at the same position with both surface and functional validation. The C-terminal APEX2 fusion (L3/L4) and the intracellular linker-FLAG (L5) are cytoplasmic and are recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion for LRP6, so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: APEX2 appended to the cytoplasmic tail of full-length Lrp6; the C-terminus (residue 1613) lies in the intracellular domain (1395–1613) and is not accessible from the extracellular face.

Linker FLAG tag immediately preceding the C-terminal APEX2 enzyme in the Lrp6-APEX2 construct; this FLAG is intracellular (between the TM domain and APEX2) and distinct from the extracellular N-terminal VSV-G tag in the same construct.
